paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus finished what He started with this man's eyes. After the first touch the man could see, but not clearly, and Jesus didn't call it good enough and walk off. He touched his eyes once again, and then "he could see everything clearly" (Mark 8:25). When a first press comes out smudgy, I don't toss the stamper, and I'm just a stamper!

Look at how close Jesus stays the whole time. He takes the man by the hand (Mark 8:23). He asks, "Can you see anything?" (Mark 8:23). The man gives an honest answer, and Jesus keeps going from there (Mark 8:24-25). So if parts of God's Word still look fuzzy to you, don't hide it. Keep coming back, because being fuzzy doesn't push you out of His hands.

At the end, Jesus sends the man home and says, "Do not go back into the village." (Mark 8:26). Mark doesn't tell us why, so I'm not going to guess. What I can say is that the man has clear sight when Jesus sends him home (Mark 8:25-26). That's the kind of baker I want you to be: keep coming back to the Word, and trust Jesus to bring things into focus.
